subject: Re: Atlas AI - Dedicated node fit & timing for pilot
messages:
From: Eva Martinez <eva@atlas.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@atlas.ai
Date: 2026-03-05T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool ask for pilot (US + EU + APAC)

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a paid pilot that runs inference for our multi-region product. High-level ask: a dedicated capacity proposal that guarantees sustained throughput for the pilot across US and EU, and a lightweight standby in APAC for lower-latency tests.

Key constraints from our side:
- Expected steady-state: ~250 r/s of short-chat generation (avg 40 tokens) in US and EU during business hours.
- Peak bursts: up to 1,200 r/s for brief windows (3-6 hours) when models retrain.
- APAC: small footprint, 30 r/s steady with occasional spikes to 200 r/s.
- We need isolation (no co-tenancy) and SOC2 evidence for the pilot.

I've attached our capacity profile and a brief SLO doc. Can you propose a region-specific node fit (GPU types, counts), onramp timeline, and a cost estimate for a 90-day pilot? Also flags for any limitations or recommended fallbacks.

We'd like a first-pass back by next Friday, 2026-03-13.

Best,
Eva Martinez
Head of Infrastructure
Atlas AI

Attachments: atlas_capacity_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet), atlas_pilot_slo.pdf (pdf)

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-06T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool ask for pilot (US + EU + APAC)

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Atlas' ask. High priority pilot ask and they explicitly want multi-region sizing + SOC2 isolation. Please see attachments (profile + SLO).

Questions to resolve for first-pass:
1) Node fit by region: propose GPU class (A100-80GB vs 4090/RTX class quantized) and counts to meet steady-state + headroom for bursts while respecting latency SLOs.
2) Can we offer APAC as standby (cross-region routing + failover) or does Atlas want localized dedicated nodes?
3) Timeline: what's the fastest we can provision a minimal dedicated pool in EU and US and a small standby in APAC (include validation window)?
4) Compliance: list of SOC2 artifacts we can attach for pilot (evidence, isolation diagrams, audit logs retention).

Ben — can you run a quick cost estimate w/ the following assumptions: 90-day pilot, 24/7 steady-state utilization (but bursts only 6 hours/day for 5 days/week), and include incremental cost for hot standby in APAC?

Karthik — can you propose the runtime config (batching, KV cache hints, quantization suggestions) so we can optimize GPU count?

I'll synthesize and send Atlas a one-pager.

--
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-09T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool ask for pilot (US + EU + APAC)

Irene / team — ran an initial sizing/cost delta. Notes below (summary, numbers are rough orders of magnitude for the one-pager):

Summary sizing recommendation (first-pass):
- US (primary): 4 x A100-80GB nodes (reserved) configured with continuous batching and 128-token KV cache per connection. Expected steady-state headroom: 300 r/s, burst handling up to ~1,100 r/s with short latency bump.
- EU (primary): 3 x A100-80GB nodes. Slightly lower steady-state, same config.
- APAC (standby): 1 x q4_0 80GB quantized node (cost-efficient) + cross-region routing. Warmed KV cache strategy during planned test windows.

Tradeoffs & caveats:
- Using A100 class in US/EU gives predictable latency and simplifies SOC2 isolation; using heavy quantization for APAC reduces cost but may increase generation variance for edge cases.
- To hit 1,200 r/s sustained we'd need additional ephemeral burst capacity (GPU burst pool) — recommended contract add-on or a canary fallback to a slightly larger non-dedicated fleet.
- If Atlas requires strict geo-residency for APAC, standby must be promoted to primary and we need 2 x A100-80GB instead of the quantized node.

Estimated 90-day pilot cost (monthlyized):
- US reserved pool (4 A100): $112k / month
- EU reserved pool (3 A100): $84k / month
- APAC standby (1 quantized 80GB): $8k / month
- Burst-on-demand buffer: $22k / month (estimate, depends on usage)
- One-time onboarding & SOC2 evidence package: $12k
-> Total estimated pilot cost (90 days): ~$645k (rounded).

I'll attach a simple cost sheet. We should present a conservative topology w/ optional burst add-on.

Ben Carter
Senior Portfolio Analyst, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: atlas_capacity_estimate_v1.csv (internal)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-12T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool ask for pilot (US + EU + APAC)

Team — I'm attaching the runtime recommendation text we should include in the Atlas one-pager. Also calling out implementation timeline and next steps below.

Runtime config (recommended):
- Model variant: open-llm-compatible 13B for pilot (lower token cost, predictable memory); allow Atlas to toggle to 70B for specific test windows.
- Batching: continuous batching window = 8ms, max batch size tuned to 48 for US/EU pools. APAC quantized node: batching window = 12ms.
- KV cache: prefix caching for chat sessions, 128-token warm cache per active session; prewarming during scheduled test windows reduces burst latency by ~35%.
- Quantization profile: use q4_0 for APAC standby; for US/EU prefer fp16 or nf4 depending on model build to avoid quality regressions.

Provisioning timeline (fastest realistic):
- Contract SOW signed -> 7 days to reserve hardware and set up networking (US/EU).
- SOC2 evidence bundle (pilot-level) assembled -> 3 business days (we have template artifacts).
- APAC standby via quantized node (in partner data center) -> 10 business days to provision and validate cross-region routing.
- End-to-end validation & dry-run -> 2 days.

Next steps / asks for the one-pager to Atlas:
1) Confirm whether APAC requires geo-residency for production (if yes, we swap quantized standby to 2 x A100 and update cost).
2) Confirm target peak window cadence (which days/hours) so we can recommend burst SLA and buffer size.
3) Approve the proposed pilot budget range and the optional burst add-on.

I'll draft the one-pager and send to Irene for final review before we share.

—
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
